idea: Weekend sourdough baking classes in Valencia, €45 a seat

mia.title: Weekend sourdough classes in Valencia
mia.one_liner: Bake your first real sourdough in three hours, and take the starter home.

brief.concept: Three-hour hands-on sourdough classes for 8 people, Friday evening and weekends, in a rented shared kitchen in Ruzafa, €45 a seat.
brief.for: Valencians aged 25 to 45 who bake at home, follow bread accounts, and have failed a starter at least once.
brief.goal: Sell 24 paid seats across three test classes before committing to a monthly kitchen slot.

checklist.task: Interview 15 home bakers about their last loaf
checklist.how: Ask in two baking groups what they baked last, what failed, what they paid to learn.
checklist.done_when: 15 logged; 6+ paid for a class or kit

checklist.task: Price three shared kitchens in Ruzafa
checklist.how: Ask for weekend half-day rates, oven count and equipment included.
checklist.done_when: Three quotes; one under €40 an hour

checklist.task: Bake the class recipe four times, timed
checklist.how: Run the full 3-hour class plan at home with a stopwatch.

checklist.task: Run a free pilot class for six friends
checklist.how: Teach the full class and ask each person what they would change.

checklist.task: Choose the name and photograph the pilot
checklist.how: Pick one of Nova's names; shoot hands, dough and the finished loaves.

checklist.task: Open three dated classes for booking
checklist.how: Publish one Friday evening and two Saturday morning dates on the page.

checklist.task: Publish the first three launch posts
checklist.how: Show the pilot class, the starter, and the dates.
checklist.done_when: Three posts live; every DM answered

checklist.how: Message interviewees and pilot guests; ask each to bring one friend.

checklist.task: Decide: book a monthly kitchen slot
checklist.how: Compare seats sold and repeat interest with break-even.
checklist.done_when: Decision written down with the numbers

leo.headline: Sell the starter that survives, not the lesson.
leo.summary: Home bakers already spend on kits and flour, and most failed sourdough fails at the starter. A small hands-on class that sends you home with a living starter answers that exact failure.

signals.name: Demand
signals.why: Home baking stayed a common weekend hobby

signals.name: Competition gap
signals.why: Few small hands-on classes; most are demos

signals.name: Price acceptance
signals.why: €40–€60 is typical for a 3-hour food class

signals.name: Channel

signals.name: Timing

leo.why_go: The failure point (the starter) is the product: a class that ends with a living starter and a support chat has a clear reason to pay.

risks.risk: Kitchen rent rises with weekend demand.
risks.mitigation: Book a fixed monthly slot only after 24 seats sell.

risks.risk: Bakers learn once and never return.
risks.mitigation: Test a €30 follow-up class on shaping and scoring.

risks.risk: Summer heat empties July and August.
risks.mitigation: Plan a two-month summer break into the numbers.

leo.next_step: Interview 15 home bakers this week: 6 who already paid to learn is the bar.

market_facts.fact: Hands-on food classes in Spanish cities commonly cost €40 to €60 for about three hours.
Shared commercial kitchens are usually rented by the hour or half-day.
Classes of 6 to 10 people are typical when everyone works their own dough.
Most beginner sourdough failures trace back to an inactive starter.

competitors.name: Online video courses
competitors.note: Cheap, but nobody checks your dough

interviews.who: Home bakers in Valencia who have tried sourdough
interviews.where: Two local baking groups and a weekend flour market
questions: Tell me about the last bread you baked.
What went wrong the last time a loaf failed?
What have you paid to learn baking so far?
Where did you look for help when it failed?
What happened to your last starter?
interviews.good_sign: They describe a dead starter in detail and have already paid for a course or kit.

kill_criteria: Stop if fewer than 6 of 15 bakers have paid to learn before.
Stop if under 12 of 24 seats sell in two weeks of promotion.
leo.verdict_rule: Go from 7.0 with no signal at 3 or below · Pivot 5.0–6.9 · No-go under 5.0

confidence.note: Desk estimates only, no web sources: signals capped at 7.5. Interviews decide.

memo.purpose: Hands-on weekend sourdough classes for home bakers in Valencia, ending with your own loaf and a living starter.
memo.problem: Home bakers try sourdough, the starter dies, and they give up. Videos can't look at your dough, and pro courses run on weekdays at school prices.
memo.insight: The starter is where beginners fail, so it is the product. A small class that sends you home with a living one solves the exact failure.
memo.verdict_line: Go, to test: break-even is 9.1 seats a class day, and the plan reaches 14 by month 12.
